evals.name: multiharness-config
evals.prompt: /implement --config — I drive this skill from both Claude Code and Codex depending on what I'm doing. When I'm running in Claude Code I want the code review done by opus. When I'm running in Codex I want the code review done by gpt 5.6 sol. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: A valid AGENTS_CONFIG.yml whose code_review phase resolves to opus on a claude_code host and gpt-5.6-sol on a codex host, plus a resolved-config summary naming the detected host.
assertions: AGENTS_CONFIG.yml is written and parses as valid YAML
Config expresses per-host routing (a host/binding axis), not a single flat runner list
code_review resolves to opus when the host is Claude Code
code_review resolves to gpt-5.6-sol when the host is Codex
No active (non-comment) command uses the removed --full-auto flag; explaining in prose why the flag is dead is correct and must not be penalized
Any Codex command shown with a prompt payload delivers the brief via stdin rather than as a bare filename argument (vacuously true if the run only shows abbreviated fragments)
The response states which harness/host was detected and shows the resolved routing

evals.name: v1-migration
evals.prompt: I already have an implement config in this repo but I want to add Codex to it — I want gpt-5.6-sol doing my code reviews when I'm working in Codex. Also can you sanity-check the existing config while you're in there, something about it feels off.
evals.expected_output: The v1 config migrated to the per-host schema with a Codex code_review binding on gpt-5.6-sol, and an explicit callout of the two latent defects in the original (--full-auto no longer exists; a bare {TASK_FILE} arg sends Codex the filename as its prompt).
assertions: Final AGENTS_CONFIG.yml parses as valid YAML
No active (non-comment) command in the final config still uses --full-auto; quoting it in a comment to explain what was fixed is correct, not a failure
The response explicitly identifies --full-auto as invalid on the current codex-cli
The response explicitly identifies the bare {TASK_FILE} argument as sending Codex the filename instead of the brief
code_review has a Codex binding on gpt-5.6-sol
The pre-existing Claude routing (opus review, sonnet build) is preserved rather than silently changed

evals.name: codex-transport
evals.prompt: I'm about to drive /implement from inside Codex rather than Claude Code for this repo. Before I do — walk me through exactly what each phase will resolve to, and show me the literal shell command you'd run to spawn the code review agent and the implementation agent. I want to paste those commands into my terminal myself to check they work.
evals.expected_output: A resolved table for all seven phases under the Codex host, plus literal codex exec commands that actually parse against codex-cli 0.147.0, deliver the brief on stdin, and use a read-only sandbox for review vs workspace-write for implementation.
assertions: All seven phases appear in the resolved table
The code review command invokes codex exec with the gpt-5.6-sol model
No command contains the removed --full-auto flag
Commands deliver the brief via stdin (trailing - with a redirect or pipe) rather than a bare file path
code_review uses a read-only sandbox and implementation uses workspace-write
Every emitted command parses successfully against the installed codex-cli argument parser

evals.name: update-v2-to-v3
evals.prompt: /implement --update — I set this config up a while back and I think it's out of date now. Bring it current, but don't change any of the models I picked.
evals.expected_output: Config moved to version 3 with every pre-existing model choice preserved byte-for-byte in meaning; new harness options explained; drift reported; only genuinely user-owned decisions asked.
assertions: Final config declares version 3

Behavioural equivalence: every phase resolves to the same runner as before on each host the v2 config already covered (moving a Claude binding from claude_code: to any: is correct — it preserves those hosts and only adds coverage elsewhere)
The response explains what is new since v2 rather than reciting a full changelog
Drift in the original config is reported (stale shell binding that now has a first-class type)
The shell binding for a now-first-class CLI is offered for conversion rather than silently rewritten
The response does not ask about purely mechanical changes such as bumping the version number

evals.name: new-harness-routing
evals.prompt: I also drive this from Cursor and sometimes Grok. Add them to my implement config — Cursor should use composer-2.5 for building and Grok for building too. Put the code review on the strongest thing available in each.
evals.expected_output: cursor and grok bindings added as first-class types with no command templates, and an explicit warning that Grok has no enforced read-only mode for the review phase.
assertions: cursor and grok bindings use first-class types (type: cursor / type: grok), not type: shell with a command template
No hand-written command: template is introduced for either harness
The response warns that Grok has no headless read-only mode before putting it on code_review, or routes review elsewhere on that host
The binary checked for Cursor is cursor-agent rather than cursor

Resolution on the hosts the config already covered (claude_code, codex) is unchanged; any behaviour change on other hosts — such as narrowing a shell binding that sat on any: — is explicitly disclosed rather than made silently
